items.followUp: Define energy and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Awards credit for the definition of work.
rubric.description: Defines work as the product of force and displacement in the direction of the force.
rubric.how: Look for the relationship between force and displacement, including the direction condition.

rubric.why: Awards credit for identifying the SI unit.
rubric.description: States that the SI unit of work is the joule (J).
rubric.how: Check that the unit is identified as the joule.

modelAnswer: Work is the product of a force and the displacement produced in the direction of the force.
The SI unit of work is the joule (J).

items.followUp: What is a solar panel? State one use.

accept: converts solar energy into electrical energy
rubric.why: Awards credit for explaining what solar cells do.
rubric.description: States that solar cells convert solar energy or sunlight into electrical energy.
rubric.how: Look for the conversion from sunlight or solar energy to electrical energy.

rubric.why: Awards credit for giving a valid use.
rubric.description: Gives a valid use, such as providing electrical power in satellites or calculators.
rubric.how: Check that at least one practical application is named.

modelAnswer: Solar cells are devices that convert sunlight directly into electrical energy.
They are used to provide electrical power in artificial satellites.

items.followUp: Define one kilowatt and express it in watts.

rubric.why: Awards credit for the definition of watt.
rubric.description: Defines one watt as a rate of doing work of one joule per second.
rubric.how: Look for the relationship 1 W = 1 J/s or an equivalent verbal definition.

rubric.why: Awards credit for naming larger units of watt.
rubric.description: Names larger units of watt, such as kilowatt and megawatt.
rubric.how: Check that at least one larger unit is named.

modelAnswer: Watt is the power when one joule of work is done in one second.
Larger units of watt include kilowatt (kW) and megawatt (MW).

items.followUp: A mass of 300 g occupies a volume of 150 cm³. Find its density in kg/m³.

rubric.why: Awards credit for correctly expressing the mass and volume in SI units.
rubric.description: Converts the given mass and volume to SI units.
rubric.how: Check for mass 0.5 kg and volume 2 × 10⁻⁴ m³, or the original values before conversion.

rubric.why: Awards credit for using density = mass/volume and obtaining the result.
rubric.description: Calculates density as 2500 kg/m³ (equivalently 2.5 g/cm³).
rubric.how: Check the density formula or its substitution and the correct density value with a unit.

modelAnswer: Given: mass, m = 500 g = 0.5 kg; volume, V = 200 cm³ = 2 × 10⁻⁴ m³.
Formula: density, ρ = m/V.
Substitution: ρ = 0.5 kg ÷ (2 × 10⁻⁴ m³).
Answer: ρ = 2500 kg/m³.

rubric.why: Awards credit for using the Fahrenheit-to-Celsius conversion relation.
rubric.description: Uses the correct conversion formula.
rubric.how: Look for C = (F − 32) × 5/9 or an equivalent form.

rubric.why: Awards credit for correct substitution and conversion.
rubric.description: Obtains approximately 37.8°C.
rubric.how: Check for the correct Celsius result with its unit.

modelAnswer: Given: temperature, F = 100°F.
Formula: C = (F − 32) × 5/9.
Answer: 100°F ≈ 37.8°C.

items.followUp: Derive the third equation of motion using a speed-time graph.

rubric.why: Awards credit for relating displacement to the area under the speed-time graph.
rubric.description: Uses the area of the trapezium under the speed-time graph to represent displacement.
rubric.how: Look for displacement expressed as the area under the graph or as average speed multiplied by time.

rubric.why: Awards credit for the average-speed expression for displacement.
rubric.description: Writes displacement as s = (u + v)t/2.
rubric.how: Check for the correct equation using initial speed, final speed and time.

rubric.why: Awards credit for using the first equation of motion to replace time.
rubric.description: Uses v = u + at, hence t = (v − u)/a.
rubric.how: Look for the correct relation between u, v, a and t.

rubric.why: Awards credit for reaching the second equation of motion.
rubric.description: Derives s = ut + ½at².
rubric.how: Check that the final equation is correct.

modelAnswer: Displacement s is the area under the speed-time graph.
The area is that of a trapezium: s = ½(u + v)t.
From the first equation of motion, v = u + at, so t = (v − u)/a.
Substituting for v in s = ½(u + v)t gives s = ½(u + u + at)t.
Therefore, s = ut + ½at², the second equation of motion.

items.followUp: Two perpendicular forces of 6 N and 8 N act on an object. Find the magnitude and direction of their resultant.

rubric.why: Awards credit for recognizing the geometry of the two components.
rubric.description: Identifies that the components act at right angles.
rubric.how: Look for a statement that the components are perpendicular or at 90°.

rubric.why: Awards credit for the Pythagorean relation for the resultant.
rubric.description: Relates the resultant magnitude to the perpendicular components using Pythagoras' theorem.
rubric.how: Check for the correct squared-component relationship or its square-root form.

rubric.why: Awards credit for the magnitude formula.
rubric.description: Gives the magnitude of the resultant as √(Fₓ² + Fᵧ²).
rubric.how: Look for the square root of the sum of the squares of the components.

rubric.why: Awards credit for finding the resultant's direction.
rubric.description: Gives the direction relation tan θ = Fᵧ/Fₓ.
rubric.how: Check for the correct ratio of perpendicular components to determine the angle.

modelAnswer: Let the perpendicular force components be Fₓ and Fᵧ.
The resultant force R is the diagonal of the right-angled triangle formed by the components.
By Pythagoras' theorem, R² = Fₓ² + Fᵧ².
Therefore, the magnitude is R = √(Fₓ² + Fᵧ²).
If θ is measured from Fₓ, its direction is given by tan θ = Fᵧ/Fₓ, so θ = tan⁻¹(Fᵧ/Fₓ).

items.followUp: A person pushes a box with a force of 200 N through 30 m in 20 s. Find the power used.

rubric.why: Awards credit for correctly identifying the given quantities.
rubric.description: Identifies force, displacement and time from the question.
rubric.how: Check for 300 N, 50 m and 60 s.

rubric.why: Awards credit for the work relation.
rubric.description: Uses work = force × displacement.
rubric.how: Look for W = Fd or its verbal equivalent.

rubric.why: Awards credit for calculating work done.
rubric.description: Calculates work as 15 000 J.
rubric.how: Check for the correct substitution and work value with unit.

rubric.why: Awards credit for the power relation.
rubric.description: Uses power = work/time.
rubric.how: Look for P = W/t or its verbal equivalent.

rubric.why: Awards credit for the final power.
rubric.description: Obtains power equal to 250 W.
rubric.how: Check for the correct numerical answer and watt unit.

modelAnswer: Given: force, F = 300 N; displacement, d = 50 m; time, t = 60 s.
Formula for work: W = Fd.
Substitution: W = 300 N × 50 m = 15 000 J.
Formula for power: P = W/t.
Substitution: P = 15 000 J ÷ 60 s = 250 W.
Answer: The power used is 250 W.
